lawyer:
SR Karmaker, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner.
Md. Nurul Huq with Shamim Khaled Ahmed, Advocate ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Rabindra Narayan Gope ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Nani Gopal Gope and others ----- Opposite parties
full_judgment:
This Rule arising out of an order of the appellate Court made on March 17,1986 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 254 of 1982 from an order of the executing Court dated April 22, 1982 gives rise to an important question of law for consideration. The question is whether the lower appellate Court was legally competent to direct the Executing Court to proceed with an Execution Case which was disposed of by the Executing Court by the order under appeal on the ground that the decree was fully satisfied as one of the decree-holders got delivery of possession of the disputed building on the reasoning that no appeal lies from such order of the Executing Court. 

 2. Mr. SR Karmaker contends that in view of provision of section 47 CPC the appeal being incompetent the impugned order of the appellate Court was without jurisdiction and the remedy of the opposite parties lies in a properly constituted separate suit and not in the execution case under Order 21 rule, 15 CPC as the dispute between the decree-holders was not a question between the parties to the suit as contemplated in section 47 CPC. His second contention was that the decree having been fully satisfied by delivery of possession of the disputed building to the petitioner the execution case was rightly disposed of on the ground of satisfaction of the decree as the delivery of possession to the petitioner was for the benefit of all the several joint decree-holders-opposite parties. Mr. Karmaker places the relevant laws and cites a number of decisions in support of his contentions which will be referred to at the relevant place in this judgment. 

 3. In repelling the contentions of Mr. Karmaker, Mr. Md. Nurul Huq submits that the appeal at the instance of the opposite parties was competent and the decree not being satisfied in terms of the order of the Court but beyond that in collusion with the judgment-debtor Saleha Khatun there was no satisfaction of the decree in law the Execution Case No. 14 of 1981 before the Subordinate Judge was competent to determine the dispute between the petitioner and the opposite-parties-decree-holders and no separate suit is necessary as suggested by Mr. Karmaker. He has also invited my attention to several decisions in support of his contentions. 

 4. To answer the points mooted at the bar it is necessary to state the relevant facts of the case. The opposite parties and the petitioner who are full brothers instituted Title Suit No. 101 of 1966 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka against sole defendant Salcha Khatun, the predecessor of the opposite parties No. 3 to 3(b), for specific performance of contract in respect of the disputed two storyed building on the basis of a registered deed of reconveyance executed on April 2, 1956. On transfer to the Court of Subordinate Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 147 of 1968. On April 21, 1981 the suit was decreed ex pane and the defendant was directed to execute and register the deed of sale in favour of the plaintiffs on receipt of Tk. 8,275.00 within 60 days. The petitioner deposited the money on May 15, 1981 on behalf of the decree-holders. The decree-holders-opposite parties also by depositing the said amount on July 17, 1981 started Execution Case No. 14 of 1981 on behalf of all the joint decree holders under Order XXI rule 15 CPC. The Court on July 27, 1981 on the prayer of opposite parties directed the judgment-debtor Salcha Khatun not to deliver the possession of the building to anybody other than the decree-holders. But inspite of the said order Salcha Khatun executed a deed of sale in respect of the building on commission obtaining the balance consideration money from the petitioner on 27.7.1981 and delivered possession of the building to the petitioner alone. Thereafter the executing Court on 22.4.1982 disposed of the execution case holding that the decree is fully satisfied and to proceed with the execution case will be abuse of the process of the Court. 

 "All questions arising between the parties to the suit in which the decree was passed, or their representative, and relating to the execution, discharge or satisfaction of the decree, shall be determined by the Court executing the decree and not by a separate suit." 

 "(1) Where a decree has been passed jointly in favour of more persons than one, any one or more of such person may unless the decree imposes any condition to the contrary, apply for the execution of the whole decree for the benefit of them all, or, where any of them has died, for the benefit of the survivors and the legal representatives of the deceased. 

 (2) Where the Court sees sufficient cause for allowing the decree to be executed on an application made under this rule, it shall make such order as it deems necessary for protecting the interests of the persons who have not joined in the application." 

 6. Mr. Karmaker relying upon section 47 submits that the expression "the parties to the suit" used in section 47 means either the defendant or the plaintiff and not, as in the present case, the plaintiffs inter se i.e. to say in this case the decree-holders and the present dispute being a dispute between the decree-holders inter se relating to the satisfaction of the decree the same is to be decided only in a properly constituted separate suit and not in Execution Proceeding under Order 21, rule 15 CPC as the expression "parties to the suit" does not contemplate decree-holders inter se the appeal was incompetent. He relied upon the case of Munshi Rai Vs. Rap Narain and others, AIR 1927 Pat, 288 wherein it has been held that where a question arises between the decree-holders with regard to payment of compensation to a decree-holder who purchased certain property in auction in execution of a decree obtained by all the decree-holders such question is not between the parties to the suit but is a question between the decree-holders as such the order made by the Court for payment of compensation to the purchasing decree-holders on setting aside the sale on payment of the decretal amount by the judgment debtor is not an order under section 47 CPC and therefore no appeal lies from such order. He also cited the decision in the case of Bans Rai Singh Vs. Krishna Chandra AIR 1981 All. 280 wherein a Single Judge held that dispute between the decree-. holders inter se and question between them do not fall under section 47 and is foreign to the scope of section 47 CPC. The decisions cited by Mr. Karmaker are quite distinguishable from the facts of the instant case before me. In none of the decisions the decree was satisfied in violation of the Order of injunction issued by the Court. Where the decree is satisfied in violation of the order of the executing court during pendency of the Execution case, as in the present case, it seems to me that such satisfaction of the decree being violative of the order of the court cannot be construed to be a satisfaction of the decree pursuant to the Court's order. In the instant case during pendency of the Execution Case No. 14 of 1981 the judgment-debtor Saicha Khatun delivered possession of the building on receipt of the consideration money from the petitioner and the petitioner after obtaining the delivery of possession gave an undertaking to the effect that Saleha Khatun shall not be liable to the decree-holders present opposite parties and he himself shall be held responsible in the event of any objection to be raised by them with regard to the satisfaction of the decree. Inviting my attention to such undertaking Mr. Karmaker contends that the petitioner is bound by such undertaking and would be responsible for satisfaction of the decree and the petitioner having obtained the delivery of the building for the benefit of other decree-holders the decree is fully satisfied and the order impugned before me has no legal foundation as the appeal before the lower appellate Court was incompetent and the Executing Court correctly disposed of the execution case on the ground that the decree has been fully satisfied. The contention does not impress me as the conduct of the petitioner also betrays a total lack of his willingness to part with the respective shares of the decree-holders opposite-parties till today. Not only the petitioner got delivery of possession of the building against the order of the Court but his conduct in not handing over possession of the building to the opposite parties No. 1 and 2 does not call for disposal of the execution case by the executing Court. 

 7. Now the question remains to be resolved is whether the appeal before the Additional District Judge in the instant case was incompetent in view of the expression "parties to the suit" used in section 47 CPC. It is difficult for me to put such a narrow construction to words "the parties to the suit" as suggested by Mr. Karmaker relying on the decisions cited by him referred to above only to mean either the plaintiff or the defendant. The words "parties to the suit" are of wide connotation and it also means, in my opinion, either the plaintiffs inter se or the defendants inter se as well. I am fortified in this view by the decision in the case of Valchand Gulabchand Shah Vs. Manekbai Hirachand Shah and others, 1953 Born. 127 relied by Mr. Huq wherein it has been held that in a fit case the Court may allow other decree-holders to intervene in pending execution if it is not properly conducted. In that case it has been, after reviewing a large number of decisions of different High Courts held that payment to one of the several joint decree-holders cannot be recognised as a payment to all unless he is authorised to receive such payment on behalf of all and does not amount to 'pro tan to satisfaction even to the extent of what is regarded to be the share in the decree of the decree-holder who received payment. It was further held therein that it is not correct to say that the remaining decree-holders can maintain the 'darkhast' only to the extent of their own shares in the decree but the remaining decree-holders are entitled to execute the whole decree. Therefore, on the strength of this decision, I hold that even where the dispute regarding discharge, satisfaction and execution of a decree arises between the decree-holders inter se the dispute can be determined by the executing court and no separate suit is necessary. In one of the earliest decisions in the case of Moti Ram Vs. Nannu Prashad, 26 All. 335 Aikman, J. took the similar view. It was held that one of the two or more joint decree-holders is not competent without having been authorised by others to certify the satisfaction of the decree by payment out of court the entire decree. This case is somewhat similar to the instant case. In the instant case before me the opposite parties did not authorise the petitioner to certify satisfaction of the decree by delivery of possession of the building. In view of my discussion above and in the light of the aforesaid principles of law laid down in Valchand Gulabchand Shaha and Moti Ram referred to above I am of the opinion that where other joint decree holders do not authorise the decree holder who receives the delivery of possession of the decretal building the decree can not be said to have been satisfied and the execution case at the instance of the other decree holders can be proceeded with according to law and the other joint decree-holders need not file a separate suit. As the dispute in the instant case relates to satisfaction of the decree although the dispute is between the decree-holders inter se, I am of the opinion that there was no satisfaction of the decree as the certificate by the petitioner of the satisfaction of the decree out of Court was not valid satisfaction as the same was done not in terms of the Court's order, rather in violation of the order of injunction and the dispute in the instant case as to satisfaction of the decree being a question between the decree-holders is to be determined by the Executing Court and the appeal before the Additional District judge was competent and the impugned order was not made without jurisdiction as suggested by Mr. Karmaker. So far as the filing of separate suit is concerned I am also of the view that the satisfaction of the decree was not in compliance with the order of the court and being out of the Court in collusion with the judgment debtor without there being any authority given to the petitioner by the opposite parties Nos.1 and 2 to take delivery of possession of the building the other joint-decree holders should not be compelled to institute a separate suit unnecessarily as suggested by Mr. Karmaker which I think rather would be abuse of the process of the Court and the question regarding satisfaction of the decree in the present case must be decided in the Execution Case No. 14 of 1981 as the question between the decree-holder relates to execution, discharge and satisfaction of the decree falls within the purview of section 47 CPC.
